title: agkit CLI output envelope, version 1
description: The CLI-OWNED wire envelope every `agkit` machine-mode document is (T-205 deliverable 2, T-225 C-S5). It is NOT the management-plane contract: `packages/shared/contract/**` is frozen, immutable and owns the server wire; this document owns the shape the CLI itself mints around whatever the server said, and it is versioned by `ENVELOPE_VERSION` (packages/cli/src/contract.ts), not by `management_version`. AUTHORED SOURCE OF TRUTH, NOT A GOLDEN: no generator emits it, no regen script owes it, and it must never be derived from `src/core/output/serialize.ts` or `envelope.ts` — a schema generated from the serializer could not detect the serializer drifting, which is the whole reason this file exists. Its drift teeth are `envelope-schema.test.ts` (C-S7), which binds every const and every property name here back to those two modules by a DIFFERENT mechanism (a source-text read) than the one that produced them. RECORDED RESIDUAL (T-225 B5.8 / R10): the `$id` host `schemas.agkit.cloud` publishes NO documents — this URL resolves to nothing today. The URL is kept deliberately, because it is the same naming grammar every `outputSchemaId` in the command registry already mints (`https://schemas.agkit.cloud/cli/v1/{noun}.{verb}.output.json`), and inventing a second, non-URL identity scheme for this one document would fork that grammar rather than repair it. Closure paths, both owner decisions and neither taken here: publish a CLI schema bundle at that host, or demote the whole family to opaque identifiers. Cross-ref T-228.

success.title: success envelope
success.description: Minted by `buildSuccessEnvelope` (envelope.ts). CLOSED: the discriminator against the error member is the PRESENCE of `data` versus `error`, never an `ok` boolean, and closedness on both branches is what makes that discrimination total — an object carrying both keys matches NEITHER branch, so the root `oneOf` fails it. Mutual exclusivity is therefore a consequence of this keyword, not a separate rule.

version.description: The envelope-schema version. MUST equal `ENVELOPE_VERSION` in packages/cli/src/contract.ts; C-S7 asserts that binding, so bumping one without the other reddens.

data.description: The handler payload — ANY JSON value, including null (`mcp serve` returns `{ data: null }`). Deliberately unconstrained: the CLI does not own the shape of management DTOs, the frozen contract does. Annotation-only, so it asserts nothing.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices carried alongside a successful payload. Present only when non-empty (envelope.ts omits the key for an empty array).

partial.description: A truncated page. DERIVED by `buildSuccessEnvelope` from an explicit `meta.partial` or the presence of `meta.next_cursor`, and lifted to a top-level envelope fact — it is never a passthrough `meta` key. `true` is the only legal value: the key is absent otherwise, never `false`. This is the envelope side of exit 3.

meta.description: Contract facts (`envelope_version` / `management_version`) or pagination facts (`next_cursor`). Present only when non-empty, and never carrying `partial` or the shown-once control marker — the serializer deletes both.

error.title: error envelope
error.description: Minted by `buildErrorEnvelope` (envelope.ts). CLOSED at the top level for the same discrimination reason as the success member; the inner `error` object is deliberately OPEN — see its own description.

version.description: The envelope-schema version. Same binding to `ENVELOPE_VERSION` as the success member's.

error.description: OPEN on purpose (`additionalProperties: true`), and this is not laziness: `ErrorEnvelope["error"]` in envelope.ts carries an index signature `[key: string]: unknown` for teachable extras — `available_fields` on `unknown_field`, and its siblings. Closing this object would make every future teachable extra a schema edit, and would reject documents the shipped CLI emits today. C-S7 asserts the bijection: this `true` holds exactly while that index signature exists.

code.description: The stable machine code a consumer branches on.

message.description: Human prose. Never load-bearing for a consumer.
